name: Deer Crossing
spec: yellow diamond with a black leaping-deer symbol
meaning: Deer often cross here, especially at dawn and dusk.

snippets.back: Wildlife-crossing warnings call for attention to deer or caribou entering the roadway unexpectedly.
Warning signs also flag slippery-when-wet pavement, a narrow bridge, cattle crossings and deer crossings.

Watch for animals especially in rural and mountain areas and between dusk and dawn, when about ninety percent of deer and elk crashes happen, and slow down and look on entering a marked animal crossing.
A deer-crossing warning calls for watching both sides of the road for deer.
Animal odds fall with dawn-and-dusk care, heed of crossing signs, woods, and water, roadside scans for eye shine, and October-through-December deer watch.
Deer behavior is unpredictable; an animal standing beside the road may run toward traffic when startled rather than away from it.
Deer top Iowa wildlife crashes, peaking in October, November, and May yet striking year-round in groups that demand extra scanning.
Be alert at deer-crossing signs, which identify areas with a history of deer-vehicle collisions.

result.summary: Meaning supported by warnings to watch for deer entering roadway and dusk-to-dawn risk; no snippet describes shape/color/symbol.
